scenes.headline: How predicting several tokens trains and speeds a model
scenes.sub: Multi-token prediction: Meta's objective, DeepSeek's modules, and self-speculative decoding.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Buzz! Most language models learn one thing: predict the next token. Multi-token prediction asks for several, and gets two wins from it. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: From each position, predict the next n tokens instead of one: a denser training signal, and extra heads that double as a built-in draft model.
scenes.say: From each position, predict the next few tokens instead of one. You get a denser training signal, and extra heads that double as a built-in draft model.

steps.say: Keep one shared transformer trunk. It turns the context into a latent at each position.
Attach several output heads. Head one predicts the next token, head two the one after, and so on.

steps.note: n loss terms per position, not one
steps.say: Their losses are summed, so every position gets several training signals instead of one. The heads run one at a time, so memory stays flat.

left.title: Meta: parallel heads
left.say: Meta's heads predict in parallel, independently. Cheap, and you can drop them to get an ordinary model back.

right.title: DeepSeek-V3: sequential modules
items: Each module sees the previous depth's token
right.say: DeepSeek-V3 chains small modules instead, each seeing the token before it. The drafts hang together better, at more cost.

scenes.title: The heads become a draft model

items.say: At inference, the extra heads draft the next few tokens cheaply.
The model checks them all in one batched pass.
It keeps the longest correct run. A rejected draft falls back to the true next token, so the output never changes.

scenes.title: Self-speculative decoding speedup
scenes.note: DeepSeek-V3's second token is accepted 85–90% of the time
scenes.say: Meta reports about three times faster decoding on code. DeepSeek-V3, drafting one extra token that's accepted most of the time, gets about one point eight.

scenes.text: One change, two payoffs: a denser training signal, and a free draft model whose speed is guaranteed lossless.
scenes.say: One change, two payoffs: a denser training signal, and a free draft model. And the speed never costs accuracy.

recap: Predict n tokens from every position
Draft, verify, keep the correct prefix
scenes.say: To recap: predict several tokens, pick your flavour of head, and let the heads draft for free.
